record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README only; the linked paper was not provided, and the code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes comparing aligned models with publicly released refusal-ablated descendants for vulnerability-analysis tasks. It reports defensive-utility outcomes, but no results on refusal behavior or on the removal of a refusal direction.
record.gate_note: The abstract reports comparative vulnerability-analysis and repair-validation results for aligned and abliterated models. It does not report a refusal test or an intervention performed by this repository.
record.test_reason: The study uses publicly released abliterated descendants of Gemma and Qwen to compare defensive security-task utility against the aligned originals. The supplied README reports no refusal rates and no direction measurement or intervention, so no result bears on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: evaluations of security assistants should jointly measure whether models respond, whether usable responses are correct, and whether outputs stay actionable across the workflow.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes an AI-generated proof-of-concept implementation. It evaluates publicly released refusal-ablated descendants but does not state or test the ablation procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: Abliterated Gemma yields more usable, applied and compiled patches (67.8/65.0/32.8% vs 29.9/24.9/9.0%). Abliterated Qwen improves line F1 (2.08→3.91%) and Top-1 accuracy (4.10→6.95%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-ablated same-lineage models can show higher defensive security-task utility than their aligned counterparts, at least partly through fewer refusals.

record.problems: Only the README abstract is available here; exact model checkpoints, uncertainty estimates, and details of the evaluation are not stated. The README describes the implementation as AI-generated and proof-of-concept.
record.rows_left_out: No additional outcome rows are reported in the supplied README abstract.

missing.what: Response or refusal rates of Aligned vs Abliterated models across prompt framings (neutral, authorization context, terminology density). The abstract implies these are measured ('whether models respond'). They would bear on V2 in released abliterated models.
